thread:
Anna Chen: quick sync — large enterprise (FinSys) just demo'd competitor X. they asked for exact feature parity on: tool-calling + structured outputs + per-route latency SLAs. they said parity is a blocker for procurement.
Mike Alvarez: noted. do we have a short list of what 'exact parity' means here? sometimes customers conflate UI niceties with infra level features.
Sophia Patel: from the demo notes: 1) function/tool calling with deterministic JSON outputs, 2) per-route 95p latency guarantees, 3) embedding compatibility/shape exactly like their existing vendor.
Vivek Rao: embedding shape is usually just a schema trick (we can map), but the function-calling determinism is tougher — needs schema enforcement + eval harness.
Olivia Martin: procurement escalation if we don't ship quick. suggested path: ship a parity shim (API-compatible surface) for the call surface, but behind the scenes route to Redwood variants. cheaper to do than full runtime parity.
Anna Chen: proposal: two-track scope. Track A (quick parity shim): 4 weeks — API aliasing + schema validation + regression tests + docs. Track B (differentiator): 12 weeks — deterministic function outputs, route-level SLA config, cost-controls, and a 'compatibility mode' for embeddings.
Mike Alvarez: resource ask? Track A is mostly product + docs + small infra. Track B needs runtime work (deterministic sampling, KV cache determinism), batcher changes, and canary infra for per-route SLA enforcement. estimate: Track A = 1 PM + 1 eng + 0.2 QA, Track B = 1 PM + 3 eng + 1 infra + 0.5 QA.
Sophia Patel: customer acceptance criteria if we do Track A: 1) API request mapping passes their integration tests, 2) no more than 2ms median added latency, 3) docs and migration guide. For Track B launch criteria: 95p latency target < 250ms for small gen, deterministic function output regression < 1% changed tokens, embedding vector shape match tests.
Vivek Rao: question on determinism: do we aim for bit-for-bit identical output or for 'functional equivalence'? bit-for-bit is impossible across model variants; functional equivalence requires evals and golden testsets. recommend functional equivalence + explicit warning in docs.
Anna Chen: leaning same. procurement won't accept a 'warning' forever. need a roadmap commitment to get function parity in 3 months. we could promise Track A in 4 weeks and Track B deliverables in 3 months.
Olivia Martin: pricing/commercial ask — if we promise parity quickly, legal will want concessions. maybe offer a limited pilot discount contingent on acceptance tests.
Mike Alvarez: ops note: to support per-route SLAs we need routing policy layer + metrics hooks + fallback policies. that's a minor platform lift but requires coordinated rollout with eng-platform.
RolloutBot: Deploy scheduled: canary for 'parity-shim' API alias will be created at 2026-05-10T08:00Z.
Sophia Patel: can we reduce scope of Track B to a prioritized subset? e.g., deterministic function outputs + canary SLA for one route (FinSys prod) first, then generalize. cuts initial eng work by ~30%.
Vivek Rao: +1 on prioritizing single-route rollout. also requires dedicated KV-cache pinning for that route during canary to avoid cross-route variance.
Anna Chen: decision checkpoint: do Track A immediately. for Track B, we'll prioritize deterministic function output + single-route SLA for FinSys as earliest deliverable. I'll take action to move budget from Q3 NICE-to-HAVEs to accelerate this into Q2.
Mike Alvarez: sprint impact — pushing Track B into Q2 pulls one backend head from other infra work. call out risks to infra roadmap in weekly planning.
Olivia Martin: commercial plan: offer a 3-month pilot with 20% credit contingent on meeting the FinSys acceptance tests. legal to draft.
Sophia Patel: acceptance test blueprint (rough): a) 2000 synthetic function-calling prompts, b) compare structured outputs via strict schema validator, c) measure latency distribution, d) embedding shape/format tests. pass if schema failures < 0.5% and latency 95p < target.
Vivek Rao: dev checklist for Track A (parity-shim): - API aliasing layer (routes) - request/response adapter - schema validation library - integration test harness with customer's test suite - doc migration guide
Anna Chen: dev checklist for Track B (determinism + SLA): - sampling seed determinism layer (configurable) - schema-led output verifier in runtime - route-level metrics and SLAs - canary & rollback automation - internal eval harness & golden dataset
Mike Alvarez: ask to eng-platform: can we reserve a small canary pool for FinSys? if yes, we'll need capacity reservation and SLA monitoring.
Olivia Martin: path to signoff: successful canary for 1 week + customer integration smoke + legal/pilot agreement signed.
Anna Chen: OK, actions: 1) Anna to send prioritized scope doc today, 2) Mike to confirm eng availability by EOD, 3) Sophia to draft acceptance test harness, 4) Olivia to start commercial pilot terms with legal. we'll reconvene Wed.
Mike Alvarez: confirmed I'll reply after standup with availability.
Sophia Patel: I'll start a test corpus and post initial pass rates here.
Vivek Rao: I'll prototype the seed-determinism switch and share notes.
Olivia Martin: looping in sales for FinSys deal thread.
Anna Chen: thanks all. quick note: we should track success metrics post-launch: customer integration time, conversion rate from pilot to paid, latency SLO attainment, and regression rate on structured outputs.
Mike Alvarez: +1, add cost-per-call delta too.
Sophia Patel: posting test harness link shortly — will drop results in this thread. :rocket:
RolloutBot: Canary: parity-shim v0 created at 2026-05-10T08:00Z (canary-id: cs-20260510-01).
